newsitem.title: USA: Overbought U.S. stocks seen opening lower.
newsitem.headline: Overbought U.S. stocks seen opening lower.

text.p: Wall Street stocks, overbought and weary from the market's strong run, are expected to move lower at the opening in an attempt to absorb recent gains.

Analysts said, however, that much would depend on the September consumer price index due ahead of the open and seen increasing by 0.3 percent with an equal rise in the core rate, according to a Reuters poll of U.S. economists.
"The market is overbought and tired, and the first order of business is to resolve this extreme," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.
"It is hard to press upward when you have already done so. We have to digest these gains," Wachtel said.
Compaq Computer Corp, Ford Motor Co, Rubbermaid Inc and Bausch & Lomb Inc were among the companies which reported earnings this morning and all three came in above expectations.
Is that good enough? Wachtel says it may not be.
"The stocks rose so much ahead of the reports that unless you have a blow-out like Intel Corp, the Street isn't going to romance you. It may take you down," Wachtel said.
In Tokyo, The Nikkei Average was down 33 at at 21,397.
in London, the FTSE 100 Index was down 21 at 4030.

Among U.S. shares traded in London, Intel, which gained $3-1/2 to $111-1/8 in New York after reporting a 40 percent rise in third-quarter profits, slipped $1/4 to $110-7/8 in London. Among other technology stocks, IBM continued to weaken, losing 3/8 to $129-1/8. GM shed $1/4 to $51-7/8, Chrysler was down $1/8 at $33-1/4 and Ford was off $1/8 at $33. Eastman Kodak was down $1/4 at $78-3/4.
The long bond was was down 3/32 to yield 6.85 percent.
The dollar dipped in Europe and remained bullish in Tokyo.

The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street writes that some on Wall Street expect David Johnson, head of Campbell Soup Co, to tell the company's annual meeting next month whether he will stay on after his contract expires in July.

The New York Times Market Place writes that arch-rival Coca-Cola Co and PepsiCo Inc released earnings on the same day for the first time in 20 years and that the reports called attention to the fact that both companies had disappointing quarters.
